title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Shop Drawing. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Shop Drawing
options.lineage: machinist's orthographic drawings with a title block
options.thesis: Every job is drawn up like a part on a shop drawing: dimensioned, numbered, and made in El Paso.
options.viewport: Phone-first: a title-block strip on top, a huge condensed headline, the castle print framed by dimension lines, the Franklins drawn as an elevation profile at the base, Get a Quote in orange.
options.risk: Can read like a cold engineering firm unless the copy stays plain-spoken and the photos stay big.

raised.raise: Motion registers in one fixed print order everywhere: frame, linework, photo, type last.
Orange marks only the one action or active state on screen, never decoration.
Layout snaps to whole modules of the sheet grid; no fractional spacing.
Form states print as annotations on the drawing, never as toasts.
A fixed ink set of sheet, line, orange, sand; any other tone is a mix of those.

options.label: Franklin Contours
options.lineage: USGS topographic quad of the Franklin Mountains
options.thesis: A 3D print is a stack of contour lines, and so is the Franklins topo map; the site is drawn as one.
options.viewport: The Franklins as stacked contours filling the hero, building up line by line; headline on the summit; photos sit on the map like survey markers.
options.risk: Topo-line backgrounds are a worn web decoration, and this is the most familiar way to say 'local + 3D'.

options.label: Dong Ho Woodblock
options.thesis: The page prints colour block by colour block, keyblock last.
options.viewport: One centred print subject with each colour layer registering in order.
options.case: Fuses as a layer metaphor, but El Paso locals do not know it and it leans crafty.
options.risk: Crafty and culturally remote for this audience.
options.kept: A fixed print order for every reveal.

options.label: Hand-processed 16mm
options.thesis: Prints shown as frames on a scratched, light-leaked strip.
options.viewport: A film strip of print photos with an orange leak on the active frame.
options.case: Pretty, but it says 'film', not 'we make your part'.
options.risk: Effects bury the prints and slow phones.
options.kept: One accent reserved for the active frame.

options.label: Azulejo Hall
options.thesis: Sections as framed tile panels in cobalt on white.
options.viewport: A tiled panel with the business name in a cartouche.
options.case: Talavera is local, but it fights the dark pin and reads like a gift shop.
options.risk: Light ground breaks the brief; souvenir feel.

options.label: Phosphor Terminal
options.thesis: The shop as a terminal transcript.
options.viewport: A blinking prompt asking what you want printed.
options.case: Exactly the sci-fi look the owner ruled out.
options.kept: States print themselves instead of popping up.

options.label: Four-shade Handheld
options.thesis: Four greens and a dither for everything.
options.viewport: A pixel sprite printer on a tiled field.
options.case: Novelty with no tie to printing or El Paso; dithers the photos.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark maker-shop landing page with a photo hero and a card grid, executed cleanly.
canonCard.viewport: Headline and two buttons over the castle photo, service cards below.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other print shop's site.
